title: Study Repeated Patterns of Misjudgment
coreMove: Treat a persuasive live decision as a pattern candidate before deciding it is a special case.
sourcePressure: The source says judgment bends under recurring pressures: fear, reward, status, uncertainty, reciprocity, fairness, conformity, missing information, and the desire to stay consistent after public commitment. Charlie Munger's two-track analysis asks what interests govern the situation and what subconscious influences may be distorting judgment.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version is naming biases after the fact or using labels to sound smart. The stronger move is catching a pressure pattern early enough to change the review.

sourceAnchors.name: Charlie Munger
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar names Munger's two-track analysis: one track asks what rational interests govern the situation, and the other asks what subconscious influences may be distorting judgment.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Munger's two-track check belongs beside the live decision, while the claim still feels reasonable and before consistency starts protecting it.

sourceAnchors.name: The Pilot's Checklist to Avoid Fooling Ourselves
sourceAnchors.detail: The source headings include this checklist framing and the notes say Munger recommends major psychology models as a checklist for complex outcomes.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A pilot checklist is useful because the familiar step disappears precisely when the cockpit starts to feel routine.

hook: A bad decision looks unique until...
Most people think mistakes are random...
You are biased and do not know it
counterintuition: The mistake is not the mistake, it is...
The real problem is not intelligence
tryThisNow: Pause for 60 seconds and think carefully
Ask yourself if you are biased

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: hospital device purchasing committee reviewing a monitor recall
exampleSpecs.audience: Sarah, a clinical operations director who already defended last quarter's vendor choice in public
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether sunk consistency keeps a weak device contract alive through another patient-safety review
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sarah draws two columns on the agenda packet, one for interests and one for distortions, then writes the recall rate under evidence instead of letting the room reopen the old defense speech
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a stapled recall notice sliding across a glossy hospital committee table

exampleSpecs.domain: municipal flood-risk update after a popular levee promise
exampleSpecs.audience: Mathieu, a deputy mayor facing residents who applauded the original plan
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether public commitment prevents revision before spring melt exposes the weak assumption
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Mathieu circles the snowpack number on the engineer's map and asks what would have to be true for the old promise to remain safe
exampleSpecs.firstImage: wet boot prints drying beside a rolled floodplain map

exampleSpecs.domain: seed-stage venture memo where one charismatic founder dominates the evidence
exampleSpecs.audience: Anke, an associate who likes the founder and knows the diligence file is thin
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether social admiration turns into an investment memo that hides missing information
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Anke asks the partners to predict what evidence would make them pass, then opens the empty customer-reference folder after each prediction
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an empty customer-reference folder on a laptop screen

exampleSpecs.domain: eldercare scheduling text thread after three repeated sibling fights
exampleSpecs.audience: Diego, an adult son trying not to repeat last month's defensive exchange
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a familiar conflict loop makes the next medical appointment harder for their father
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Diego prints the last three text threads, marks the same sequence in each one, and sends one reset question before answering the latest accusation
exampleSpecs.firstImage: three printed text threads spread beside a pharmacy receipt

exampleSpecs.domain: university replication lab deciding whether to publish a surprising pilot result
exampleSpecs.audience: Aanya, a doctoral student whose supervisor is excited by the finding
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a desired result and group excitement hide the missing alternative explanations
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Aanya asks the lab to name two mundane explanations before anyone writes the result into the abstract
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "What else would make this graph jump?" written beside a projector glow

exampleSpecs.domain: nonprofit emergency grant panel after one emotional applicant video
exampleSpecs.audience: Ben, a program officer who feels the room leaning toward the visible case
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether one vivid story crowds out the quieter applications with stronger documented need
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Ben asks each panelist to score the file once with the video hidden and once after viewing it, then compares the swing before a vote
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You watch a thumbnail freeze on a paused applicant video

skillTargets: spot public commitment before it hardens
use Munger's two-track review on a live choice
recognize when a bias label is replacing review

tryThisNowSpec: Take one live decision and draw two columns: interests in the situation and pressures in your own judgment. Put one concrete item in each column before you act.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
